name: Permission Calculator
description: Convert between symbolic and octal file permissions and list what each permission class means.

hints.mode: Accepts octal such as 755, the nine-character symbolic form such as rwxr-xr-x, or the long form such as u=rwx,g=rx,o=r.
hints.bits: Checked bits override the matching class of the permission value; a class with nothing checked keeps the value from the permission value.
hints.output: The result gives both the octal and the symbolic form and breaks down read, write and execute for every class.

faq.q: Why are setuid, setgid and the sticky bit not handled?
faq.a: The tool only covers the low nine permission bits; special bits are out of scope, so 4755 is treated as 755.

faq.q: How do I express "others have no permissions at all"?
faq.a: The permission-bit interface cannot zero a class — checking nothing means "keep the permission value". To clear it, write the symbolic form directly, for example rwxr-x---.
Octal is convenient for chmod commands, the symbolic form is easier to read; both forms and the per-class breakdown are always shown.
